           kubectl -n dci-acme get secret dci-acme-superuser -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d
  Backups: NONE — no WAL archiving and no base backups for this instance, so no point-in-time restore is possible
  Root-key escrow: /home/op/.devicechain/escrow/acme-rootkey.escrow
                   copy this off the machine and store the passphrase separately — it is the ONLY copy of the key outside the cluster, and no database backup contains it

DeviceChain is up. Open the web console at https://devicechain.local/ and sign in.
  Local cluster: map the host first — add "127.0.0.1 devicechain.local" to /etc/hosts (or bootstrap with --host localhost).
  The TLS cert is self-signed (dev-grade), so your browser will warn once (or use --no-tls).
  A client that should verify it trusts the instance's CA instead: kubectl -n dci-acme get secret devicechain-tls -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d
note: with MQTT fail-closed off, sustained MQTT overload can drop already-acknowledged events from the capture stream. --mqtt-fail-closed prevents it (at a lower ingest ceiling): https://docs.devicechain.io/concepts/security-model#accepted-gaps
